[Doc] Document /inference/v1/generate request/response fields and DP rank header (#62305)

Signed-off-by: aoshen02 <aoshen@inferact.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

files.patch:
@@ -1,8 +1,50 @@
 # Tokens In <> Tokens Out API
 
-`/inference/v1/generate` takes prompt token IDs and returns generated token IDs. It is the generation step of the `render → generate → derender` pipeline used in disaggregated serving (see the [Renderer APIs](renderer.md) and [Derenderer APIs](derenderer.md)).
+`POST /inference/v1/generate` is the token-in/token-out (TITO) HTTP endpoint: it takes prompt token IDs and returns generated token IDs, logprobs keyed by integer token ID, and `finish_reason`/`stop_reason`, with no detokenization. Use it when the caller does its own tokenization and chat templating, such as an RL rollout worker. It is also the generation step of the `render → generate → derender` pipeline used in disaggregated serving (see the [Renderer APIs](renderer.md) and [Derenderer APIs](derenderer.md)).
 
-The endpoint is registered on `vllm serve` with `--enable-scale-out`, and always with `--tokens-only`. `--tokens-only` also skips loading the tokenizer, so the server can't turn token IDs back into text.
+## Enabling the endpoint (`--enable-scale-out`, `--tokens-only`)
+
+- `--enable-scale-out` registers it, with `/render`, `/derender` and `/inference/v1/abort_requests`.
+- `--tokens-only` always registers it, skips loading the tokenizer and forces `detokenize=False`. Stop strings (`sampling_params.stop`) are then rejected with a 400; use `stop_token_ids`.
+- With neither flag, it returns 403 `Scale-out endpoints are disabled. Restart vllm serve with --enable-scale-out to enable them.`
+
+```bash
+vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enable-scale-out
+
+curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/inference/v1/generate \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  -d '{"token_ids": [151644, 872, 198], "sampling_params": {"max_tokens": 32, "logprobs": 1}}'
+```
+
+A full client is in [examples/scale_out/token_generation_client.py](../../../examples/scale_out/token_generation_client.py).
+
+## Request fields
+
+| Field | Notes |
+| --- | --- |
+| `token_ids` | Required `list[int]`: the already-templated prompt. Non-empty, no negative IDs. |
+| `sampling_params` | Required. Any [SamplingParams](../../api/README.md#inference-parameters) field, e.g. `max_tokens`, `temperature`, `logprobs`, `stop_token_ids`. Without `max_tokens`, the server applies its own default (as on the OpenAI endpoints), not 16. |
+| `output_mode` | `"tokens"` (default) or `"text"`, see [Output modes](#output-modes). |
+| `stream`, `stream_options` | SSE chunks ending with `data: [DONE]`. |
+| `return_token_ids` | Echo the final prompt IDs as `prompt_token_ids`. |
+| `features` / `content_parts` | Multimodal input, mutually exclusive. |
+| `request_id`, `model`, `cache_salt`, `priority`, `kv_transfer_params`, `ec_transfer_params` | Optional. |
+
+## Response fields
+
+| `choices[i]` field | Notes |
+| --- | --- |
+| `token_ids` | Generated token IDs. |
+| `finish_reason` | `stop`, `length` or `abort`. |
+| `stop_reason` | Stop token ID or string; `null` on EOS, length and abort. |
+| `logprobs` | `{"content": [{"token_id", "logprob", "rank", "top_logprobs": [...]}]}`, one entry per token, sampled token first. `token_id` is an integer, not the older `"token_id:<id>"` string. Needs `sampling_params.logprobs`. |
+| `weight_versions`, `routed_experts`, `sampling_mask` | Optional, see [Weight versions](#weight-versions); the last two need `--enable-return-routed-experts` / `--return-sampling-mask`. |
+
+The top level adds `request_id`, `usage`, `prompt_token_ids` and `prompt_logprobs`. Stream chunks carry the same per-choice fields for the new tokens.
+
+## Targeting a data-parallel rank (`X-data-parallel-rank`)
+
+Send the header `X-data-parallel-rank: <int>` to pin a request to one data-parallel (DP) engine rank; there is no body field. Without the header, or with a non-integer value, the request is load balanced. A rank outside `[0, data_parallel_size)` is rejected.
 
 ## Output modes

@@ -18,6 +18,8 @@ The following open-source RL libraries use vLLM for fast rollouts (sorted alphab
 
 For weight synchronization between training and inference, see the [Weight Transfer](weight_transfer/README.md) documentation, which covers the pluggable backend system with [NCCL](weight_transfer/nccl.md) (multi-GPU) and [IPC](weight_transfer/ipc.md) (same-GPU) engines. To verify that an update landed on every rank, see the [Weight Checker](weight_checker.md).
 
+For MoE policies, see [Routed Experts Return](routed_experts.md) (`--enable-return-routed-experts`) to get the per-token expert routing of each rollout for routing replay (R3) in the trainer.
+
 For pipelining generation and training to improve GPU utilization and throughput, see the [Async Reinforcement Learning](async_rl.md) guide, which covers the pause/resume API for safely updating weights mid-flight.
 
 See the following notebooks showing how to use vLLM for GRPO:

@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+# Routed Experts Return (MoE Routing Replay / R3)
+
+`--enable-return-routed-experts` makes vLLM return the routed experts (the expert IDs each MoE layer's router selected) for every token of a request. RL trainers use it for MoE routing replay (R3): the training forward pass reuses the rollout's routing.
+
+```bash
+vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --enable-return-routed-experts
+# offline: LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B", enable_return_routed_experts=True)
+```
+
+The flag sets `AuxOutputConfig.enable_return_routed_experts` (full form: `--aux-output-config '{"enable_return_routed_experts": true, "max_bytes": N}'`). There is no per-request on/off switch.
+
+## Requirements
+
+Startup fails with a `ValueError` unless:
+
+- **Model Runner V2** is used (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` if vLLM falls back to V1);
+- the runner is `generate` and the model is **MoE**;
+- **prefix caching is enabled** (the default). `--no-enable-prefix-caching` fails; the old v0.21 advice to disable it is wrong.
+
+Rejected at startup: adaptive speculative verification, PP > 1, DCP/PCP > 1, and the `NixlConnector`, `NixlPullConnector`, `NixlPushConnector`, `MoRIIOConnector`, `MooncakeConnector` KV connectors. Regular speculative decoding works.
+
+### How it works: aux output connector
+
+Routing is stored by the aux output connector (`vllm/distributed/aux_output_connector/`, configured via `--aux-output-config`), keyed by KV block hash and shared with prefix caching, which is why prefix caching is required. `max_bytes` is its host-memory LRU capacity (default: derived from KV cache capacity). If a prefix-cache hit needs evicted rows, the worker raises `BlockObjectStoreError`; increase `max_bytes`.
+
+## Output format
+
+| API | Field |
+| --- | --- |
+| Offline (`LLM`, `AsyncLLM`) | `CompletionOutput.routed_experts`: `np.ndarray` or `None` |
+| `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` | `choices[i].routed_experts`: base64 `.npy`, **non-streaming only** |
+| `/inference/v1/generate` | `routed_experts` per choice (base64 `.npy`); with `stream: true`, on the final chunk |
+
+- **Shape:** `(num_tokens - 1 - routed_experts_prompt_start, num_moe_layers, num_experts_per_tok)`, `num_tokens` = prompt + output. The last sampled token has no row.
+- **Rows:** row `i` is position `routed_experts_prompt_start + i` of `prompt_token_ids + output_token_ids`.
+- **dtype:** `uint8` for at most 256 experts, else `uint16`; logical expert IDs.
+- Filled only when the request finishes. `None` if the flag is off or the request aborted before any forward pass.
+
+```python
+import base64, io
+import numpy as np
+
+experts = np.load(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(choice["routed_experts"])))
+```
+
+## `routed_experts_prompt_start`
+
+Per-request, default `0`: drops the first N prompt-token rows (e.g. routing already received in earlier turns). Must be `0 <= value <= prompt_len`, else HTTP 400. Pass it top-level on `/v1/*completions`, inside `sampling_params` on `/inference/v1/generate`, or as `SamplingParams(routed_experts_prompt_start=...)`.
+
+## Limitations
+
+- The Rust HTTP frontend never returns `routed_experts` and always sends `routed_experts_prompt_start = 0`. Use the Python API server.
+
+Example: [examples/rl/routed_experts_e2e.py](../../examples/rl/routed_experts_e2e.py).

@@ -466,6 +466,31 @@ This approach is more robust than index-based access (`messages[0]`, `messages[1
 
 Example template file: [examples/pooling/score/template/nemotron-rerank.jinja](../../../examples/pooling/score/template/nemotron-rerank.jinja)
 
+#### Templates declared by Sentence Transformers checkpoints
+
+vLLM does not apply a checkpoint's chat template by default, since many rerankers inherit an unrelated template from their base LLM. The exception is a Sentence Transformers (v5.4+) `CrossEncoder` with a single `sequence-classification` Transformer module whose `sentence_bert_config.json` declares the `message` modality. Sentence Transformers formats the pairs of such checkpoints as `query`/`document` messages, so vLLM does the same with the saved template:
+
+```json
+{
+    "transformer_task": "sequence-classification",
+    "modality_config": {
+        "text": {"method": "forward", "method_output_name": "logits"},
+        "message": {"method": "forward", "method_output_name": "logits", "format": "flat"}
+    },
+    "module_output_name": "scores",
+    "processing_kwargs": {"chat_template": {"add_generation_prompt": true}}
+}
+```
+
+- The default chat template is used, unless `processing_kwargs.chat_template.chat_template` names another template saved with the tokenizer (e.g. `additional_chat_templates/score.jinja` for `"score"`).
+- The other `processing_kwargs.chat_template` settings, such as `add_generation_prompt`, are passed to the template; the request's `chat_template_kwargs` override them.
+- Message contents are passed as strings, as with `--chat-template`.
+- vLLM does not restore the template suffix after truncation (`restore_suffix`). Use `max_tokens_per_doc` rather than `truncate_prompt_tokens` to truncate long documents.
+- `--chat-template` (or the `chat_template` argument of `LLM.score`) takes precedence over the saved template and its settings.
+- Models with a built-in score template keep using it.
+
+The template in use is logged at startup.
+
 ### Enable/disable activation
 
 You can enable or disable activation via `use_activation` only works for cross-encoder models.

+    Sentence Transformers formats the pairs of such checkpoints as
+    `query`/`document` messages with the saved chat template.

+        revision: Model revision to inspect.

+        `None` if the checkpoint does not declare the `message` modality.

+        transformer_config = get_hf_file_to_dict(

+        and not modules[0].get("path")
+        and isinstance(transformer_config, dict)
+        and transformer_config.get("transformer_task") == "sequence-classification"
+        and isinstance(

+## Trainer Without vLLM over HTTP
+
+A colocated trainer can speak the [HTTP endpoints](README.md#api-endpoints)
+directly, with only PyTorch and an HTTP client. The server needs
+`VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1`; without it, init and start return 200 and
+the first `/update_weights` returns 500. Reference:
+[`rlhf_http_ipc_no_vllm.py`](../../../examples/rl/rlhf_http_ipc_no_vllm.py).
+
+`POST /init_weight_transfer_engine` body: `{"init_info": {"packed": false}}`.
+
+`POST /update_weights` body `{"update_info": {...}}`:
+
+| Field | Meaning |
+| ----- | ------- |
+| `names`, `dtype_names`, `shapes` | Checkpoint names, `torch` dtype attribute names (`"bfloat16"`), full shapes |
+| `ipc_handles_pickled` | `base64(pickle.dumps(handles))`. Unpacked: a list with one dict per name. Packed: one dict for the shared buffer |
+| `tensor_sizes` | Packed only: byte size of each tensor in the chunk, in `names` order |
+
+- A handle dict is `{gpu_uuid: reduce_tensor(t)[1]}` with one entry per GPU the
+  server uses (`torch.multiprocessing.reductions.reduce_tensor`).
+  `gpu_uuid = str(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(i).uuid)`, **without** the
+  `GPU-` prefix that `nvidia-smi` prints. The worker overwrites `args[6]`
+  (device index) with its own.
+- `ipc_handles` (unpickled) is not JSON-serializable; over HTTP use
+  `ipc_handles_pickled`.
+- Packed: export one `uint8` buffer once and reuse it for every chunk. Copy
+  `t.contiguous().view(-1).view(torch.uint8)` in `names` order and close a chunk
+  **before** the next tensor would overflow it (unlike NCCL, which closes after).
+  A tensor larger than the buffer is an error. Synchronize before each
+  `/update_weights`; do not overwrite the buffer until the call returns.
+- Keep every exported tensor alive until `/finish_weight_update` returns, then
+  drop the references and call `torch.cuda.ipc_collect()`.
+- Multi-rank trainers: each rank exports handles for its own GPU, the ranks
+  gather the `{uuid: args}` dicts to rank 0 over their own `torch.distributed`
+  group and merge them per index, and rank 0 sends all HTTP. In packed mode,
+  barrier before and after each `/update_weights`.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""CUDA IPC weight sync over HTTP from a trainer that never imports vLLM.
+
+The trainer uses only `torch`, `requests`, `safetensors`, `pybase64` and the
+stdlib, and speaks the wire protocol in
+`docs/training/weight_transfer/ipc.md` ("Trainer Without vLLM over HTTP"):
+it exports its tensors with `torch.multiprocessing.reductions.reduce_tensor`
+and sends the handles, pickled and base64-encoded, in `ipc_handles_pickled`.
+
+IPC requires colocation: this process holds a full copy of the weights on every
+GPU the server uses, and keys each handle by that GPU's UUID. A multi-process
+trainer would instead gather the per-rank `{uuid: args}` dicts to one rank.
+
+Start a server; IPC handles are pickled, so it needs
+`VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1` (the weights it starts with are discarded):
+
+    VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1 \
+        CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
+        --load-format dummy --enforce-eager --gpu-memory-utilization 0.4 \
+        --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "ipc"}'
+
+Then run the trainer on the same GPU(s) (`--packed` for chunked transfer):
+
+    CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python examples/rl/rlhf_http_ipc_no_vllm.py \
+        --checkpoint /path/to/Qwen3-0.6B
+
+For a TP=2 server on GPUs 0-1, use `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1` on both sides and
+pass `--num-gpus 2` to the trainer.
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+
+class _BlockVLLM:
+    def find_spec(self, name, path=None, target=None):
+        if name.split(".")[0] == "vllm":
+            raise ImportError(f"this trainer must not import {name!r}")
+        return None
+
+
+sys.meta_path.insert(0, _BlockVLLM())
+
+import argparse  # noqa: E402
+import glob  # noqa: E402
+import pickle  # noqa: E402
+
+import pybase64 as base64  # noqa: E402
+import requests  # noqa: E402
+import torch  # noqa: E402
+from safetensors.torch import load_file  # noqa: E402
+from torch.multiprocessing.reductions import reduce_tensor  # noqa: E402
+
+parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+parser.add_argument("--url", default="http://localhost:8000")
+parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", required=True, help="dir with *.safetensors")
+parser.add_argument("--num-gpus", type=int, default=1)
+parser.add_argument("--packed", action="store_true")
+parser.add_argument("--packed-buffer-size-bytes", type=int, default=512 << 20)
+args = parser.parse_args()
+
+
+def post(path: str, body: dict | None = None) -> dict:
+    r = requests.post(args.url + path, json=body or {}, timeout=600)
+    r.raise_for_status()
+    return r.json()
+
+
+def generate(prompts: list[str]) -> list[str]:
+    model = requests.get(args.url + "/v1/models", timeout=60).json()["data"][0]["id"]
+    body = {"model": model, "prompt": prompts, "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0}
+    choices = post("/v1/completions", body)["choices"]
+    return [c["text"] for c in sorted(choices, key=lambda c: c["index"])]
+
+
+# Weights are {gpu_uuid: {name: tensor}}: one full copy per colocated GPU. The
+# UUID is str(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(i).uuid), with no "GPU-" prefix.
+Weights = dict[str, dict[str, torch.Tensor]]
+
+
+def update_weights(
+    weights: Weights,
+    names: list[str],
+    ipc_handles: list[dict[str, tuple]] | dict[str, tuple],
+    tensor_sizes: list[int] | None = None,
+) -> None:
+    w = next(iter(weights.values()))
+    update_info = {
+        "names": names,
+        "dtype_names": [str(w[n].dtype).removeprefix("torch.") for n in names],
+        "shapes": [list(w[n].shape) for n in names],
+        "ipc_handles_pickled": base64.b64encode(pickle.dumps(ipc_handles)).decode(),
+    }
+    if tensor_sizes is not None:
+        update_info["tensor_sizes"] = tensor_sizes
+    post("/update_weights", {"update_info": update_info})
+
+
+def send_unpacked(weights: Weights, names: list[str]) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    """One /update_weights call; one {uuid: args} dict per parameter."""
+    copies = {u: {n: w[n].contiguous() for n in names} for u, w in weights.items()}
+    handles = [{u: reduce_tensor(copies[u][n])[1] for u in copies} for n in names]
+    update_weights(weights, names, handles)
+    return [t for c in copies.values() for t in c.values()]
+
+
+def send_packed(weights: Weights, names: list[str], cap: int) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    """One /update_weights call per chunk; one {uuid: args} dict per chunk."""
+    buffers = {
+        u: torch.empty(cap, dtype=torch.uint8, device=w[names[0]].device)
+        for u, w in weights.items()
+    }
+    handle = {u: reduce_tensor(b)[1] for u, b in buffers.items()}  # export once
+    chunk: list[str] = []
+    sizes: list[int] = []
+
+    def flush() -> None:
+        for b in buffers.values():
+            torch.accelerator.synchronize(b.device)  # copies must land before the read
+        update_weights(weights, chunk, handle, sizes)
+        chunk.clear()
+        sizes.clear()
+
+    for n in names:
+        nbytes = next(iter(weights.values()))[n].nbytes
+        assert nbytes <= cap, f"{n} ({nbytes} B) exceeds the buffer"
+        if chunk and sum(sizes) + nbytes > cap:  # close *before* overflowing
+            flush()
+        offset = sum(sizes)
+        for u, w in weights.items():
+            flat = w[n].contiguous().view(-1).view(torch.uint8)
+            buffers[u][offset : offset + nbytes].copy_(flat)
+        chunk.append(n)
+        sizes.append(nbytes)
+    if chunk:
+        flush()
+    return list(buffers.values())
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    weights: Weights = {}
+    for i in range(args.num_gpus):
+        uuid = str(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(i).uuid)
+        weights[uuid] = {}
+        for path in sorted(glob.glob(f"{args.checkpoint}/*.safetensors")):
+            weights[uuid].update(load_file(path, device=f"cuda:{i}"))
+    names = sorted(next(iter(weights.values())))
+
+    prompts = ["The capital of France is", "def fibonacci(n):"]
+    print("before:", generate(prompts))
+
+    post("/init_weight_transfer_engine", {"init_info": {"packed": args.packed}})
+    post("/start_weight_update")
+    if args.packed:
+        exported = send_packed(weights, names, args.packed_buffer_size_bytes)
+    else:
+        exported = send_unpacked(weights, names)
+    post("/finish_weight_update", {"weight_version": None})
+    # The worker reads the exported memory until finish; only then release it.
+    del exported
+    torch.cuda.ipc_collect()
+
+    print("after: ", generate(prompts))
+    assert not [m for m in sys.modules if m.split(".")[0] == "vllm"]
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""NCCL weight sync over HTTP from a trainer that never imports vLLM.
+
+The trainer uses only `torch`, `requests`, `safetensors`, `pybase64` and the
+stdlib, and speaks the wire protocol in
+`docs/training/weight_transfer/nccl.md` ("Trainer Without vLLM over HTTP"):
+`nccl_unique_id_b64` rendezvous, a one-element warm-up `all_reduce`, then
+`/start_weight_update` -> `/update_weights` (concurrent with the rank-0
+broadcast) -> `/finish_weight_update`.
+
+The NCCL communicator is a plain `torch.distributed.ProcessGroupNCCL` over a
+private `TCPStore` that only the trainer joins. Its `ncclUniqueId` is read back
+from store key "0", which is a torch implementation detail.
+
+Start a server on GPUs 0-1 (the weights it starts with are discarded):
+
+    VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
+        --tensor-parallel-size 2 --load-format dummy --enforce-eager \
+        --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "nccl"}'
+
+Then run the trainer on GPU 2 (`--packed` for packed broadcasting):
+
+    CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 python examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl_no_vllm.py \
+        --checkpoint /path/to/Qwen3-0.6B
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+
+class _BlockVLLM:
+    def find_spec(self, name, path=None, target=None):
+        if name.split(".")[0] == "vllm":
+            raise ImportError(f"this trainer must not import {name!r}")
+        return None
+
+
+sys.meta_path.insert(0, _BlockVLLM())
+
+import argparse  # noqa: E402
+import datetime  # noqa: E402
+import glob  # noqa: E402
+import threading  # noqa: E402
+
+import pybase64 as base64  # noqa: E402
+import requests  # noqa: E402
+import torch  # noqa: E402
+import torch.distributed as dist  # noqa: E402
+from safetensors.torch import load_file  # noqa: E402
+
+parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+parser.add_argument("--url", default="http://localhost:8000")
+parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", required=True, help="dir with *.safetensors")
+parser.add_argument("--packed", action="store_true")
+parser.add_argument("--packed-buffer-size-bytes", type=int, default=64 << 20)
+parser.add_argument("--store-port", type=int, default=29612)
+args = parser.parse_args()
+
+
+def post(path: str, body: dict | None = None) -> dict:
+    r = requests.post(args.url + path, json=body or {}, timeout=600)
+    r.raise_for_status()
+    return r.json()
+
+
+class PostInBackground(threading.Thread):
+    """An HTTP call that only returns once this process joins the collective."""
+
+    def __init__(self, path: str, body: dict) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.path, self.body = path, body
+        self.error: BaseException | None = None
+        self.start()
+
+    def run(self) -> None:
+        try:
+            post(self.path, self.body)
+        except BaseException as e:
+            self.error = e
+
+    def result(self) -> None:
+        self.join()
+        if self.error is not None:
+            raise self.error
+
+
+def generate(prompts: list[str]) -> list[str]:
+    model = requests.get(args.url + "/v1/models", timeout=60).json()["data"][0]["id"]
+    body = {"model": model, "prompt": prompts, "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0}
+    choices = post("/v1/completions", body)["choices"]
+    return [c["text"] for c in sorted(choices, key=lambda c: c["index"])]
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    device = torch.device("cuda:0")
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+    weights: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
+    for path in sorted(glob.glob(f"{args.checkpoint}/*.safetensors")):
+        weights.update(load_file(path, device="cuda:0"))
+    names = sorted(weights)
+
+    prompts = ["The capital of France is", "def fibonacci(n):"]
+    print("before:", generate(prompts))
+
+    # Trainer is NCCL rank 0; vLLM worker i is rank 1 + i.
+    world_size = 1 + requests.get(args.url + "/get_world_size").json()["world_size"]
+    store = dist.TCPStore(
+        "127.0.0.1", args.store_port, is_master=True, wait_for_workers=False
+    )
+    pg = dist.ProcessGroupNCCL(store, 0, world_size, dist.ProcessGroupNCCL.Options())
+    connect = threading.Thread(target=pg.eager_connect_single_device, args=(device,))
+    connect.start()  # publishes the unique id, then waits in ncclCommInitRank
+    reader = dist.TCPStore("127.0.0.1", args.store_port, is_master=False)
+    reader.wait(["0"], datetime.timedelta(seconds=60))
+    unique_id = reader.get("0")
+    assert len(unique_id) == 128
+
+    init = PostInBackground(
+        "/init_weight_transfer_engine",
+        {
+            "init_info": {
+                "nccl_unique_id_b64": base64.b64encode(unique_id).decode(),
+                "rank_offset": 1,
+                "world_size": world_size,
+                "packed": args.packed,
+                "packed_buffer_size_bytes": args.packed_buffer_size_bytes,
+            }
+        },
+    )
+    connect.join()
+    pg.allreduce([torch.zeros(1, device=device)]).wait()  # vLLM's warm-up
+    init.result()
+
+    def broadcast(t: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        opts = dist.BroadcastOptions()
+        opts.rootRank = 0
+        pg.broadcast([t], opts).wait()
+
+    post("/start_weight_update")
+    update_info = {
+        "names": names,
+        "dtype_names": [str(weights[n].dtype).removeprefix("torch.") for n in names],
+        "shapes": [list(weights[n].shape) for n in names],
+    }
+    update = PostInBackground("/update_weights", {"update_info": update_info})
+    if not args.packed:
+        for n in names:
+            broadcast(weights[n].contiguous())
+    else:
+        # Same chunking as the worker: a chunk closes right after the tensor
+        # that pushes it past the buffer size.
+        chunk: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+        size = 0
+        for n in names:
+            chunk.append(weights[n].contiguous().view(-1).view(torch.uint8))
+            size += chunk[-1].numel()
+            if size > args.packed_buffer_size_bytes:
+                broadcast(torch.cat(chunk))
+                chunk, size = [], 0
+        if chunk:
+            broadcast(torch.cat(chunk))
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    update.result()
+    post("/finish_weight_update", {"weight_version": None})
+
+    print("after: ", generate(prompts))
+    post("/shutdown_weight_transfer_engine")
+    pg.shutdown()
+
+    assert not [m for m in sys.modules if m.split(".")[0] == "vllm"]
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Check that no root-anchored `.dockerignore` entry excludes tracked files.
+
+Docker builds bind-mount `.git` but copy the working tree through the build
+context, so git sees any tracked file that `.dockerignore` drops as deleted.
+That dirty tree fails `tools/check_repo.sh` in release builds
+(`GIT_REPO_CHECK=1`) and adds a `.dYYYYMMDD` dirty suffix to the wheel version.
+
+Usage:
+    python tools/pre_commit/check_dockerignore_tracked.py
+"""
+
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+DOCKERIGNORE = Path(".dockerignore")
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    rooted = [
+        line.strip().strip("/")
+        for line in DOCKERIGNORE.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
+        if line.startswith("/")
+    ]
+    if not rooted:
+        return 0
+    tracked = subprocess.run(
+        ["git", "ls-files", "--", *rooted],
+        check=True,
+        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+        text=True,
+    ).stdout.split()
+    if not tracked:
+        return 0
+    print(
+        f"{DOCKERIGNORE} excludes {len(tracked)} tracked file(s). Docker builds "
+        "would see them as deleted and the git tree as dirty, failing "
+        "tools/check_repo.sh in release builds. First few:"
+    )
+    for path in tracked[:10]:
+        print(f"  {path}")
+    return 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+#
+# Derive everything the release pipeline needs about a ROCm stack from its base
+# Dockerfile, so the stack's image is the single input to every ROCm script.
+#
+# Usage: source .buildkite/scripts/rocm/stack.sh <base-dockerfile>
+#   e.g. docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base (ROCm 10.0) or docker/Dockerfile.rocm_72_base
+#
+# Exports:
+#   ROCM_STACK_BASE_DOCKERFILE  the base Dockerfile
+#   ROCM_STACK_DOCKERFILE       the matching vLLM Dockerfile (base name minus _base)
+#   ROCM_STACK_THEROCK          1 if the ROCm SDK comes from TheRock wheels
+#   ROCM_STACK_VERSION          ROCm version, e.g. 10.0.0 or 7.2.3
+#   ROCM_STACK_VARIANT          wheel variant and Docker Hub tag flavor from major.minor,
+#                               same rule as setup.py (rocm100, rocm72)
+#   ROCM_STACK_IMAGE_KEY        hash of the base Dockerfile (base image cache key)
+#   ROCM_STACK_WHEEL_KEY        hash of the base Dockerfile plus files it COPYs from
+#                               the repo (base wheel cache key)
+#   ROCM_STACK_ECR_BASE         ECR tag of the cached base image
+#   ROCM_STACK_ECR_IMAGE        ECR tag of this commit's release image
+#   ROCM_STACK_BASE_WHEELS_DIR  local dir for base wheels (also the artifact path)
+#   ROCM_STACK_VLLM_WHEEL_DIR   local dir for the vLLM wheel (also the artifact path)
+
+rocm_stack_init() {
+    local base="$1"
+    if [[ ! -f "$base" ]]; then
+        echo "ROCm base Dockerfile not found: $base" >&2
+        return 2
+    fi
+    ROCM_STACK_BASE_DOCKERFILE="$base"
+    ROCM_STACK_DOCKERFILE="${base%_base}"
+
+    local sdk
+    sdk=$(sed -nE 's/^ARG ROCM_SDK_VERSION=([0-9.]+).*/\1/p' "$base" | head -1)
+    if [[ -n "$sdk" ]]; then
+        ROCM_STACK_THEROCK=1
+        ROCM_STACK_VERSION="$sdk"
+    else
+        ROCM_STACK_THEROCK=0
+        # BASE_IMAGE format: rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:7.2.3-complete -> 7.2.3
+        ROCM_STACK_VERSION=$(sed -nE 's/^ARG BASE_IMAGE=.*:([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+).*/\1/p' "$base" | head -1)
+    fi
+    if [[ -z "$ROCM_STACK_VERSION" ]]; then
+        echo "Could not determine the ROCm version from $base" >&2
+        return 2
+    fi
+
+    local major minor
+    IFS=. read -r major minor _ <<< "$ROCM_STACK_VERSION"
+    ROCM_STACK_VARIANT="rocm${major}${minor}"
+
+    ROCM_STACK_IMAGE_KEY=$(sha256sum "$base" | cut -c1-16)
+    local inputs
+    inputs=$(grep -E '^COPY ' "$base" | grep -v -- '--from' | awk '{print $2}' || true)
+    if [[ -z "$inputs" ]]; then
+        ROCM_STACK_WHEEL_KEY="$ROCM_STACK_IMAGE_KEY"
+    else
+        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
+        ROCM_STACK_WHEEL_KEY=$(sha256sum "$base" $inputs | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
+    fi
+
+    local ecr="public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-release-repo"
+    ROCM_STACK_ECR_BASE="${ecr}:${ROCM_STACK_IMAGE_KEY}-${ROCM_STACK_VARIANT}-base"
+    ROCM_STACK_ECR_IMAGE="${ecr}:${BUILDKITE_COMMIT:-unknown}-${ROCM_STACK_VARIANT}"
+    ROCM_STACK_BASE_WHEELS_DIR="artifacts/${ROCM_STACK_VARIANT}-base-wheels"
+    ROCM_STACK_VLLM_WHEEL_DIR="artifacts/${ROCM_STACK_VARIANT}-vllm-wheel"
+
+    export ROCM_STACK_BASE_DOCKERFILE ROCM_STACK_DOCKERFILE ROCM_STACK_THEROCK \
+        ROCM_STACK_VERSION ROCM_STACK_VARIANT ROCM_STACK_IMAGE_KEY \
+        ROCM_STACK_WHEEL_KEY ROCM_STACK_ECR_BASE ROCM_STACK_ECR_IMAGE \
+        ROCM_STACK_BASE_WHEELS_DIR ROCM_STACK_VLLM_WHEEL_DIR
+}
+
+if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
+    rocm_stack_init "$1"
+fi

+    "torch==${TORCH_VERSION}" \
+    "torchaudio==${TORCHAUDIO_VERSION}" \
+    "torchvision==${TORCHVISION_VERSION}"
+
+# Install the AMD-compiled device kernels corresponding to PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH:
+
+# Possible values that can be in PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH:
+#
+# gfx90a (MI210/250), gfx942 (MI300), gfx950 (MI350), gfx1100 (7900XTX),
+# gfx1101 (7800XT), gfx1200 (9070XT), gfx1201 (9070), gfx1150/1151 (Strix APU)
+
+# For each arch in PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH, install the precompiled GPU code that
+# PyTorch needs to run on that specific chip.
+SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-c"]
+RUN TORCH_VER=$(python3 -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__)") \
+    && for arch in $(echo "${PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH}" | tr ';' ' '); do \
+        echo "Installing device packages for ${arch}" \
+        && pip install --index-url ${ROCM_RELEASE_WHEELS_MULTIARCH_URL} \
+            --extra-index-url ${ROCM_NIGHTLY_WHEELS_MULTIARCH_URL} \
+            "torch[device-${arch}]==${TORCH_VER}" \
+            "torchvision[device-${arch}]==${TORCHVISION_VERSION}" \

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Adapt TheRock (ROCm 10) wheels for the vLLM ROCm wheel index.
+
+repack-torch: TheRock's torch wheel hard-pins the triton it was built with.
+    vLLM ships a newer source-built triton, so rewrite that one Requires-Dist
+    and the METADATA hash in RECORD. The version and filename stay the same,
+    because torchvision and the amd-torch-device-* wheels pin torch exactly.
+
+external-links: list the TheRock wheels the index links to instead of hosting
+    (ROCm SDK, device kernels, torchvision/torchaudio, rocm-bootstrap), with
+    versions and GPU arches read from docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base. torch's
+    device-<arch> extras can also pull in a GPU-family wheel (e.g.
+    amd-torch-device-gfx110x), so those are read from the torch wheel itself.
+
+patch-amdsmi: rocm-sdk-core ships the amdsmi bindings under
+    _rocm_sdk_core/share/amd_smi, and the loader finds libamd_smi relative to
+    that directory. Once installed as its own package it would miss the SDK
+    library, so also look it up through the installed _rocm_sdk_core package.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import shutil
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import urllib.request
+import zipfile
+from html.parser import HTMLParser
+from pathlib import Path
+from urllib.parse import unquote, urljoin
+
+import pybase64 as base64
+import regex as re
+
+
+def _record_hash(data: bytes) -> str:
+    digest = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashlib.sha256(data).digest()).rstrip(b"=")
+    return f"sha256={digest.decode()}"
+
+
+def repack_torch(wheel: Path, triton_version: str, out_dir: Path) -> Path:
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(wheel) as src:
+        infos = src.infolist()
+        metadata = next(i for i in infos if i.filename.endswith(".dist-info/METADATA"))
+        record = next(i for i in infos if i.filename.endswith(".dist-info/RECORD"))
+
+        text = src.read(metadata).decode()
+        new_text, count = re.subn(
+            r"^Requires-Dist: triton\s*==\s*\S+\s*$",
+            f"Requires-Dist: triton=={triton_version}",
+            text,
+            flags=re.MULTILINE,
+        )
+        if count != 1:
+            raise SystemExit(
+                f"expected exactly one pinned triton requirement, found {count}"
+            )
+        new_metadata = new_text.encode()
+
+        lines = src.read(record).decode().splitlines()
+        prefix = metadata.filename + ","
+        replaced = [
+            f"{metadata.filename},{_record_hash(new_metadata)},{len(new_metadata)}"
+            if line.startswith(prefix)
+            else line
+            for line in lines
+        ]
+        if replaced == lines:
+            raise SystemExit(f"{metadata.filename} not found in RECORD")
+        new_record = ("\n".join(replaced) + "\n").encode()
+
+        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        out = out_dir / wheel.name
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(out, "w") as dst:
+            for info in infos:
+                if info.filename == metadata.filename:
+                    data = new_metadata
+                elif info.filename == record.filename:
+                    data = new_record
+                else:
+                    data = src.read(info)
+                dst.writestr(info, data, compress_type=info.compress_type)
+    return out
+
+
+_AMDSMI_ANCHOR = "    possible_locations.append(libamd_smi_path)\n"
+_AMDSMI_PATCH = """\
+    # vLLM: installed as its own package, find the lib in TheRock's rocm-sdk-core.
+    try:
+        import importlib.util
+        _sdk_core = importlib.util.find_spec("_rocm_sdk_core")
+        if _sdk_core is not None and _sdk_core.origin:
+            possible_locations.append(
+                Path(_sdk_core.origin).parent / "lib/libamd_smi.so.27")
+    except Exception:
+        pass
+"""
+
+
+def patch_amdsmi(src_dir: Path, out_dir: Path) -> Path:
+    out_dir = out_dir.resolve()
+    if out_dir.exists():
+        shutil.rmtree(out_dir)
+    shutil.copytree(src_dir, out_dir, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("tests"))
+    wrapper = out_dir / "amdsmi" / "amdsmi_wrapper.py"
+    text = wrapper.read_text()
+    if text.count(_AMDSMI_ANCHOR) != 1:
+        raise SystemExit(f"amdsmi loader anchor not found in {wrapper}")
+    wrapper.write_text(text.replace(_AMDSMI_ANCHOR, _AMDSMI_ANCHOR + _AMDSMI_PATCH))
+    return out_dir
+
+
+def dockerfile_args(dockerfile: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
+    args = {}
+    for m in re.finditer(r'^ARG (\w+)="?([^"\s]*)"?', dockerfile.read_text(), re.M):
+        args.setdefault(m.group(1), m.group(2))
+    return args
+
+
+class _Links(HTMLParser):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.hrefs: list[str] = []
+
+    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
+        if tag == "a":
+            self.hrefs += [v for k, v in attrs if k == "href" and v]
+
+
+def _project_files(index_url: str, project: str) -> list[str]:
+    page = urljoin(index_url, f"{project}/")
+    with urllib.request.urlopen(page, timeout=60) as resp:
+        parser = _Links()
+        parser.feed(resp.read().decode())
+    return [urljoin(page, href.split("#")[0]) for href in parser.hrefs]
+
+
+def _usable(url: str, version: str | None) -> bool:
+    name = unquote(url.rsplit("/", 1)[-1])
+    if (
+        version is not None
+        and f"-{version}-" not in name
+        and f"-{version}." not in name
+    ):
+        return False
+    if name.endswith(".tar.gz"):
+        return True
+    tags = name[: -len(".whl")].split("-")[-3:]
+    return (
+        name.endswith(".whl")
+        and tags[0] in ("cp312", "py3")
+        and (tags[2] == "any" or ("x86_64" in tags[2] and "win" not in tags[2]))
+    )
+
+
+def torch_device_requirements(
+    torch_wheel: Path, arches: list[str]
+) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
+    """(project, version) pairs that torch's device-<arch> extras require."""
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(torch_wheel) as zf:
+        metadata = next(n for n in zf.namelist() if n.endswith(".dist-info/METADATA"))
+        text = zf.read(metadata).decode()
+    wanted = {f"device-{arch}" for arch in arches}
+    reqs = []
+    for m in re.finditer(
+        r'^Requires-Dist: ([\w.-]+)\s*==\s*(\S+)\s*;.*extra == "([^"]+)"', text, re.M
+    ):
+        if m.group(3) in wanted and (m.group(1), m.group(2)) not in reqs:
+            reqs.append((m.group(1), m.group(2)))
+    missing = wanted - set(re.findall(r'extra == "(device-[^"]+)"', text))
+    if missing:
+        raise SystemExit(f"torch has no extras for {sorted(missing)}")
+    return reqs
+
+
+def external_links(dockerfile: Path, torch_wheel: Path) -> list[str]:
+    args = dockerfile_args(dockerfile)
+    index = args["ROCM_RELEASE_WHEELS_MULTIARCH_URL"]
+    sdk = args["ROCM_SDK_VERSION"]
+    vision_v, audio_v = args["TORCHVISION_VERSION"], args["TORCHAUDIO_VERSION"]
+    arches = [a for a in args["PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH"].split(";") if a]
+    wanted: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = [
+        ("rocm", sdk),
+        ("rocm-sdk-core", sdk),
+        ("rocm-sdk-libraries", sdk),
+        ("torchvision", vision_v),
+        ("torchaudio", audio_v),
+        ("rocm-bootstrap", None),
+    ]
+    for arch in arches:
+        wanted += [
+            (f"rocm-sdk-device-{arch}", sdk),
+            (f"amd-torchvision-device-{arch}", vision_v),
+        ]
+    wanted += torch_device_requirements(torch_wheel, arches)
+    urls = []
+    for project, version in wanted:
+        found = [u for u in _project_files(index, project) if _usable(u, version)]
+        if not found:
+            raise SystemExit(f"no usable {project}=={version} files on {index}")
+        urls += found
+    return urls
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
+    p = sub.add_parser("repack-torch")
+    p.add_argument("wheel", type=Path)
+    p.add_argument("--triton-version", required=True)
+    p.add_argument("--out-dir", type=Path, required=True)
+    p = sub.add_parser("external-links")
+    p.add_argument(
+        "--dockerfile", type=Path, default=Path("docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base")
+    )
+    p.add_argument("--torch-wheel", type=Path, required=True)
+    p = sub.add_parser("patch-amdsmi")
+    p.add_argument("src_dir", type=Path)
+    p.add_argument("--out-dir", type=Path, default=None)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    if args.cmd == "repack-torch":
+        print(repack_torch(args.wheel, args.triton_version, args.out_dir))
+    elif args.cmd == "external-links":
+        print("\n".join(external_links(args.dockerfile, args.torch_wheel)))
+    else:
+        out = args.out_dir or Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "amd_smi"
+        print(patch_amdsmi(args.src_dir, out))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

     return json.dumps(params, ensure_ascii=False)
 
 
+# What ends an open value in ``_PARAM_RE``: a closing tag or the next opener.
+_PARAM_VALUE_END_RE = re.compile(r"<\s*/\s*parameter\s*>|<\s*parameter\s*=")
+
+
+def _param_value_end_window(text: str) -> str:
+    """Return the suffix of *text* that may still grow into a value end."""
+    start = text.rfind("<")
+    if start == -1:
+        return ""
+    tail = text[start:]
+    return tail if _PARAM_VALUE_END_RE.fullmatch(tail, partial=True) else ""
+
+
+def _param_value_extender(
+    raw_args: str, trim_newlines: bool
+) -> ArgValueExtender | None:
+    """Extend the open trailing ``<parameter=...>`` value of *raw_args*.
+
+    The extender streams exactly what the converter would for the same text.
+    With *trim_newlines* it follows ``_trim_wrapping_newlines``: it drops a
+    leading newline of the value and holds back a trailing one.
+    """
+    match = _PARTIAL_PARAM_RE.search(_PARAM_RE.sub("", raw_args))
+    if match is None:
+        return None
+    name, value = match.group(1), match.group(2)
+    # A repeated key keeps its first position, so its value is not last.
+    if any(m.group(1) == name for m in _PARAM_RE.finditer(raw_args)):
+        return None
+
+    window = _param_value_end_window(value)
+    started = bool(value)
+    held = "\n" if trim_newlines and value.endswith("\n") and value != "\n" else ""
+
+    def extend(delta: str) -> str | None:
+        nonlocal window, started, held
+        text = window + delta
+        if _PARAM_VALUE_END_RE.search(text):
+            return None
+        window = _param_value_end_window(text)
+        if trim_newlines:
+            text = held + delta
+            if not started and text:
+                started = True
+                text = text.removeprefix("\n")
+            held = "\n" if text.endswith("\n") else ""
+            text = text[: len(text) - len(held)]
+        else:
+            text = delta
+        return json.dumps(text, ensure_ascii=False)[1:-1]
+
+    return extend
+
+
+def _qwen3_arg_value_extender(raw_args: str) -> ArgValueExtender | None:
+    return _param_value_extender(raw_args, trim_newlines=True)
+
